about.headline: WHO ARE THE BEARS
copy: Ben Johnson took over in Chicago in 2025. He took an offense that finished bottom five in the league the year before and turned it into a {top|top ten unit} in his first season.

{pts|441 points}, the third most in franchise history, second in the NFL in explosive plays, and Caleb Williams set the franchise passing record. Seven wins came while trailing in the final two minutes, the most by any team since at least 1970.
Then they won the NFC North and came back from 21 to 6 down in the fourth quarter to beat Green Bay in the playoffs.

principles.title: OUR QUARTERBACK IS THE CENTER OF EVERYTHING
principles.blurb: Caleb is a live threat on almost every snap. He reads our RPOs, pulls it to the perimeter, and throws downfield off all of it.
principles.detail: Everything in this offense runs through Caleb Williams, a live threat on almost every single snap. He reads defenders on our RPOs, pulls it and gets out on the perimeter, and throws it downfield off all of it. The defense has to account for him as a runner before it can worry about anybody else.

principles.title: MOTION AND CREATIVITY
principles.blurb: The defense never lines up against the same picture twice. Orbits, shifts, bodies across the formation on almost everything.
principles.detail: The defense never gets to line up against the same picture twice. We have motion on almost everything: orbits, shifts, guys coming across the formation. It is all about finding creative ways to get our playmakers the football with room to work.

principles.title: BUILT FOR EXPLOSIVES
principles.blurb: Second in the NFL in explosive plays. Every call carries a way to break big, and we hunt chunk plays all game long.
principles.detail: The Bears finished second in the NFL in explosive plays, and that is exactly what we are going for. We are not trying to grind out five yards at a time. Every call in this offense has a way to break a big one, and we hunt chunk plays all game long.

plays.name: RPO Alert Bubble

reads.label: Pre-Snap Numbers
reads.text: Read the bubble side defender pre-snap. If the overhang walks up inside or you have a numbers advantage on the perimeter, throw the bubble immediately.

reads.label: At the Snap :  Bubble or Hand Off
reads.text: At the snap, if the bubble-side defender stays outside and it's two-on-two, stay with the handoff. If he blitzes or jumps inside, pull and throw the bubble.

reads.label: Inside Zone Cut Decision
reads.text: On the handoff, read the defenders flowing laterally. Push it inside if they're overflowing to the perimeter, or bounce it outside if they collapse down the middle.

reads.label: Bubble Block Quality
reads.text: When throwing the bubble, confirm you have a one-on-one block on the outside. One block, one miss ,  that's the equation for a big gain or score.

adjustments: 2 TEs to wide side
Bubble to short side
RB cut back on overflow
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want to put a defender in conflict pre-snap. Two tight ends wide side, bubble short side ,  you're forcing that overhang to declare. He cheats inside, you throw it. He stays out, you hand it off and cut it up. Simple math. Don't overthink it.

plays.name: Motion Jet Touch Pass

reads.label: Box Density
reads.text: If the defense is packing the box and condensing the inside, the touch pass gets the ball to the perimeter quickly ,  take it.

reads.label: RB Lead Blocker
reads.text: Read the running back out front. Let him get to the second level before committing to a lane. Bubble out to give him room to pick up defenders.

reads.label: One-on-One Safety
reads.text: If your receiver ends up one-on-one with a safety in space, trust your playmaker to win that matchup.

adjustments: Bubble route wider for space
RB lead blocker path
Jet motion timing adjustment
plays.whenToUse: Call this when defenses start loading the box and taking away your inside run game. Gets a playmaker out in space in a hurry ,  and your RB out front as a lead blocker makes it even nastier. Works from the red zone all the way out to 15 yards.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN Jet Touch Pass Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion Jet Dash Weak

reads.label: 1st Read :  Shallow Tight End
reads.text: Primary read coming out of the boot. As you roll to the perimeter, look for the shallow crossing tight end. He gets open consistently as linebackers and flat defenders bite on the jet motion or the running back in the flat.

reads.label: 2nd Read :  Deep Tight End Post
reads.text: If the linebacker sits on the shallow cross, the deeper tight end on the post will clear the middle safety and come open over the top. The solo receiver streak helps pull back deep defenders to create that window.

reads.label: 3rd Read :  Running Back in Flat
reads.text: If pressure is in your face or the linebackers and flat defenders are dropping underneath the tight ends, dump it quick to the running back in the flat for easy yards.

reads.label: 4th Read :  QB Scramble/Keep
reads.text: If all three pass options are covered, you're already on the perimeter. Pull it and run with your athletic quarterback. Don't force it ,  take what the defense gives you.

adjustments: Slots to the wide side
Inside tight end on post
plays.whenToUse: Call this when defenses are overreacting to your jet motion and flowing hard to one side. The boot the other way punishes that aggression. Works great with an athletic QB who can threaten the edge and keep defenders honest. Mix it in alongside your jet touch pass so the motion looks identical pre-snap ,  that's where the real damage happens.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN Jet Dash WK Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: RPO Stretch Alert Lookie

reads.label: Stretch or Cutback
reads.text: Aim point is outside between the tight ends. If the defense overplays the edge and cuts off the stretch, plant your foot and cut back downhill immediately ,  don't let them be too aggressive on the perimeter.

reads.label: Backside Linebackers on RPO
reads.text: Keep eyes on the two linebackers at the snap. If they flow hard or bite aggressively toward the stretch, the backside slant opens up behind them ,  pull it and drop it in.

reads.label: Run vs. Throw Decision
reads.text: If linebackers stay disciplined and don't crash, hand off and take what the stretch gives you ,  either bounce outside or cut downhill off the double team.

adjustments: Two TEs plus inside receiver wide side
Backside slant built in
Double team seals to second level
plays.whenToUse: Call this when defenses are getting too aggressive and over-pursuing the stretch. The RPO slant punishes linebackers either way ,  they can't cheat to the edge or crash downhill without giving something up. Run it when you need a chunk play and want to put the defense in a bind.

plays.name: Return PA Z Over

reads.label: 1st Read :  Deep Cross
reads.text: Post-snap, read the user/linebacker in the middle of the field. If the return bubble motion pulls them out of position or aggressive, fire the deep crosser into the vacated middle.

reads.label: 2nd Read :  Tight End Dig
reads.text: If the linebacker flows hard with the deep cross, the tight end dig comes in right behind him into the open pocket. Drop it in where the user should have been.

reads.label: 3rd Read :  Return Route (Flat)
reads.text: If defenders are playing 10-15 yards deep or you're getting pressure, hit the return route in the flat as a quick checkdown. One-on-one in space, make a guy miss.

reads.label: 4th Read :  RB Option Route
reads.text: Against zone, the running back sits down in the open window. Against man, he options inside or out. Use as a checkdown when the dig is covered and the cross is taken away.

adjustments: RB on option route
X receiver deep cross
Return bubble motion pre-snap
Stack to wide side
plays.whenToUse: Run this off your return RPO zone alert. Once they've seen that bubble motion a couple times and they're flying to stop it, that's when you hit them with this. Middle of the field opens right up. Call it when the user is playing aggressive and leaving the middle exposed.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Return PA Z over Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Portland Y Wheel

reads.label: 1st Read :  Tight End Wheel
reads.text: Primary read is the tight end wheel up the sideline. The backside streak pulls deep defenders back while the RB flat route holds the flat defender underneath. If the flat defender stays shallow and the streak clears the deep blue defender, drop the ball in to the tight end as he cuts upfield along the sideline.

reads.label: 2nd Read :  RB Flat
reads.text: If at the snap the flat defender turns and runs with the wheel, plays too far back, or man coverage gets caught inside, immediately look to the running back in the flat. The tight end becomes a blocker out in front to help spring the gain.

reads.label: 3rd Read :  Dig (Middle of Field)
reads.text: If both the wheel and the flat are taken away ,  flat defender jumps the flat and a linebacker matches the wheel ,  look to the dig breaking into the middle of the field. Fire it into the vacated zone left by the linebacker who chased the wheel.

reads.label: 4th Read :  Hitch / Option Route
reads.text: Versus zone, if defenders are dropping back under the dig, the hitch runner sits down in the open zone rather than optioning across the field. Versus man, choose between the shallow option route or the deeper dig depending on whether the hook linebacker jumps underneath.

adjustments: Backside receiver on streak
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want to attack zone with the tight end wheel ,  it's your go-to. The streak clears the top, the flat holds the underneath, and that wheel just runs free up the sideline. Call it on third down, call it before the half, call it in the red zone. The middle-of-field options give you a built-in answer versus man so you're never wrong with this play.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Portland Y Wheel Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion Orbit Fake Swing Wheel

reads.label: 1st Read :  Tight End Wheel
reads.text: Primary read. As the orbit motion draws the linebacker down and the flat defender bites on the swing fake, the tight end releases off what looks like a block and wheels up behind the streak. If the flat defender stays shallow and the streak is pulling deep defenders back, drop it into the wheel as he cuts up the field.

reads.label: 2nd Read :  Outside Bunch Slant
reads.text: If linebackers vacate the middle chasing the motion, or if it's man coverage, look to the slant from the outside player in the bunch. The user will be pulled to the backside, giving 2-3 yards of separation to throw the slant into the vacated middle and create a run-after-catch opportunity.

reads.label: 3rd Read :  Swing Pass
reads.text: Checkdown. If at the snap everyone is getting deep and nobody is in the flat, the swing pass player is your outlet. He'll have room to operate because the defense is playing off, allowing him to catch and get upfield.

adjustments: Point man on streak route
Bunch to wide side
Auto orbit motion pre-snap
plays.whenToUse: Call this when defenses are sleeping on your swing screen ,  they've seen it enough to bite, now you make them pay. Great against aggressive linebackers who chase the motion and against man coverage where the slant becomes an easy pitch-and-catch. The orbit motion does the work for you.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN Orbit FK Swing Wheel Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion Orbit Swing Screen

reads.label: Numbers on the Perimeter
reads.text: Count blockers vs. defenders on the orbit side. If you have a numbers advantage (3 blockers vs. 3 defenders or fewer), pitch it out to the orbit motion back and let him work.

reads.label: Linebacker Aggression
reads.text: Watch the linebackers in the middle of the field. If they're crashing hard or blitzing, pull off the swing screen and hit the backside slant coming open behind them.

reads.label: Backside Slant (RPO)
reads.text: If linebackers overcommit to the orbit motion, the backside slant is pitch and catch from roughly four yards ,  take it immediately.

reads.label: Linebackers Playing Off
reads.text: If the linebackers are dropping back deep and not biting on the motion, the swing screen to the flat is available underneath.

adjustments: Bunch to wide side only
Auto orbit motion by RB
Backside slant as RPO
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want to stress the linebackers with a horizontal threat and punish them either way. They bite on the motion, you're hitting the slant. They play off, you're getting your back in space with blockers. Empty bunch to the wide side gives you the numbers to make it work.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN Orbit Swing Screen Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Drag Curl

reads.label: Z Post (Primary vs. Aggressive Underneath)
reads.text: If linebackers and flat defenders bite down on the drags and the backside streak pulls the deep defenders away from the middle, the Z post breaks inside into the vacated space. Wait for the safety to flip his hip chasing the streak, then drop it in behind him.

reads.label: Curl (vs. Cover 2 / Deep Blue Stays Home)
reads.text: If the underneath defenders are playing aggressive on the drags but the middle safety or a deep blue defender does not get pulled back by the streak, pivot to the curl route from the inside bunch player sitting down on the short side behind the flat defender and linebackers.

reads.label: Drag (vs. Man Coverage)
reads.text: Against man coverage, look immediately to the two drags crossing the field. Throw to whichever drag has the most separation as they cut across. The receiver coming from the wide side is often the cleaner option.

reads.label: Drag Sit (vs. Zone :  Linebackers Bailing)
reads.text: Against zone with linebackers and flat defenders playing off and bailing, the drag with an option route on him will sit down in the open window. Drop it in on his sit for an easy 7, 8 yard gain.

adjustments: TE on drag from bunch short side
Outside stack receiver on streak wide side
Curl route inside bunch player
Option route on drag vs zone
plays.whenToUse: Call this on third down, money situations, or anytime you need a reliable answer out of empty. It's a mesh concept at heart ,  you've got answers versus man, zone, and Cover 2. If they're playing aggressive underneath, the post is open. If they're playing back, sit the drag or the curl. You're always getting yards on this play.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Drag Curl Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: RPO Read TE Slide

reads.label: The Orbit Pulls the Flow
reads.text: Come out with the orbit player to the wide side. At the snap he comes around and shoots out the opposite way of the play ,  and that's already doing work, because it pulls the flow of the defense away from where you're actually going.

reads.label: Read the Edge
reads.text: It's a read option on the edge defender. If he crashes down, pull it with your quarterback and get out on the perimeter to make plays.

reads.label: The TE Flip
reads.text: Here's where it gets really good. Out on that edge, the second defenders start sucking in toward your quarterback, flip it to the tight end coming across the formation with blockers in front of him. Your tight end in space on the edge is where this play turns explosive.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: And if the edge defender closes it all down, just hand it off up the middle.

adjustments: Orbit player to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: This is the first play in the install for a reason. One snap gives you four answers: the give, the keep, the flip, and the perimeter. Call it early to find out how their edge wants to play you, then spend the rest of the game punishing the answer.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Orbit Rpo Read TE Slide Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Deep Flood

reads.label: Front Side :  the Flood Read
reads.text: Against zone the front side plays exactly like flood: read the flat defender. The streak runs the deep defender off, so if the flat stays shallow, hit the corner route deep down the sideline. Everybody staying back? Throw the underneath route to your tight end breaking to the flat.

reads.label: Middle :  Option and Post
reads.text: Over the middle you've got the option route and the post. Linebackers bite down on the option route, throw the post right over the top of them. Everybody plays back, hit the option route as he sits down.

reads.label: Vs Man :  Five Beaters at Once
reads.text: Two deep corner routes to work down the field, a speed out from the tight end that separates underneath, the option route breaking either way, and the post over the middle. Pick your favorite matchup.

reads.label: Vs the Blitz
reads.text: If they're bringing it, motion the backside post man into the backfield and block him instead. Everything else stays live.

adjustments: Front bunch player on a streak (vs zone)
Outside bunch receiver stemmed up one notch
Backside outside player on a post
plays.whenToUse: One of the best plays in the entire scheme, because it attacks man and zone and gives you options all over the field. Bunch to the wide side and read it out. There is no coverage this play doesn't have an answer for.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Deep Flood Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion PA X Zig Flood

reads.label: The Snap-Motion Corner
reads.text: The auto motion across the field into the corner route is what makes this play. Because he's motioning at the snap he's basically unblockable in man, and he gets great separation as he breaks it off.

reads.label: Post Over the Top
reads.text: If the linebackers and the user stay shallow, or they jump over to help on that corner route, throw the post attacking the deep middle right over the top.

reads.label: The Nasty-Split Slant
reads.text: The backside solo receiver is brought way inside on a slant. Most corners sit in an outside shade, so when he breaks across the field the separation is free.

reads.label: Seven-Man Protection
reads.text: You're blocking a tight end and a running back, so this is a seven-man protection. Call it into the heavy blitzers, block everything up, and still hit all of it down the field.

adjustments: Trips side to the short side
Outside tight end on a post
Block the running back
Backside solo receiver on a slant
plays.whenToUse: This is the go-to man beater in the offense, with an answer at every level of the field. The motion corner is the money route - and because the protection is seven men, it's also the call you make when they start sending the house.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN PA X Zig Flood Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Return RPO Zone Alert

reads.label: The Return Bubble
reads.text: At the snap you get an auto motion into the backfield and back out to the sideline as a bubble. If those defenders cheat inside or get caught inside, throw the bubble with a blocker in front and go get big yards outside.

reads.label: Slant Behind Their Heads
reads.text: If the bubble is taken away but the linebackers are jumping down on the run, throw the slant in right behind their heads.

reads.label: Hand It Downhill
reads.text: Bubble covered and the linebackers staying back on the slant? Now there's a ton of room to hand it off up the middle and let your back get downhill.

adjustments: Return route to the wide side
Backside receiver on a slant
plays.whenToUse: The engine of the run game. Three answers off one motion: the bubble, the slant, and the give. And once they start flying out to stop that bubble, Return PA Z Over is already loaded to hit the middle they just emptied.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__Return RPO Zone Alert Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: RPO QB Screen Draw

reads.label: Screen Right Now
reads.text: Right at the snap, look to the screen. Guys jumping inside, or you've got the numbers advantage out there? Drop it out with blockers in front - there should be a lot of green grass.

reads.label: The Backside Stick Combo
reads.text: Against zone, if everybody's playing back, throw the hitch or the flat - whichever you like. Against man that hitch turns into an option route, breaks to the sideline, and gets a ton of separation.

reads.label: Tuck the Draw
reads.text: If everybody stays outside on the pass, you've got a ton of room to tuck it and run up the middle on the designed draw. With a quarterback like Caleb Williams getting downhill, that's a big play every time.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: An amazing RPO that combines the quick pass game with a QB draw, and it creates a ton of problems for a defense. Screen, stick combo, or the draw - somebody is always wrong.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__RPO Q Screen Draw Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion PA Verts

reads.label: TE Corner Early
reads.text: At the snap, if the corner or the deep defender on the short side is playing back with the flat defender shallow, throw the corner route to the tight end as he breaks it inside.

reads.label: The Motioned-Over Post
reads.text: After the play action, if the linebackers suck down and hold on that tight end corner, throw the motioned-over post from your tight end in behind the linebackers for big plays.

reads.label: Slot Post Over Everything
reads.text: If the safeties and linebackers bite down and in on that motioned-over post, the slot post is going up over the top - fire it deep for the huge one.

reads.label: Checkdown and Comeback
reads.text: After the play action your running back leaks to the flat as the checkdown, and the comeback is waiting on the sideline when the flat defenders bite down.

adjustments: Two-receiver side to the wide side
Outside receiver on that side on a comeback
plays.whenToUse: An incredible deep passing play with three vertical routes attacking at once - the corner, the shallower post, and the deeper post. Call it once the run game and the RPOs have the linebackers leaning, then throw it over all of them.
plays.heroShot: art/Bears Assets__MTN PA Verts Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Motion Shuffle Verts Smash

reads.label: The Wheel Over the Top
reads.text: The auto motion sends your running back out behind the receivers on the short side, then he wheels it up the field. The streak on his side pulls the deep defender back, and as your back gets in behind the flat defender you just drop it in over the top. Huge pickup down the sideline every time.

reads.label: Quick Out to the Back
reads.text: If at the snap the flat defender is playing way back or staying inside, get it out to the running back quick as he cuts upfield.

reads.label: Post and Return Inside
reads.text: Against zone, if the linebackers drop down on the return route - or the user runs out to your back - the post is breaking in over the middle. Staying back off the post? The return route cuts in shallow underneath it.

reads.label: Vs Man
reads.text: If the running back has a step on his guy, throw the wheel up the sideline. The post and the return route both get really nice separation against man as well.

adjustments: Running back to the short side
Both outside receivers on streaks
plays.whenToUse: One of the best deep passing plays in the whole scheme, and the culmination of everything this offense is about - the motion, the creativity, and the explosive over the top. When you need the big one, this is the call.

about.headline: WHO ARE THE COMMANDERS
copy: In 2024 Jayden Daniels walked into Washington as a rookie and flipped the franchise. They went from {rec|4-13 to 12-5}, he won Offensive Rookie of the Year, and they made the deepest playoff run this team had made since 1991.
They went into Detroit and hung {det|45 on the Lions} before falling one game short of the Super Bowl. Last year got derailed by injuries and Daniels started only seven games.
Now he is back healthy for 2026 with a young, retooled roster around him, and the rookie season already showed what the ceiling is when he is on the field. That is the offense we are building.

principles.title: DEFEND HIM ON EVERY SINGLE SNAP
principles.blurb: Jayden Daniels is the most dangerous running quarterback in football, and this whole offense is built to make you deal with that on every play.
principles.detail: Jayden Daniels is the most dangerous running quarterback in football, and this whole offense is built to make you deal with that on every play. Between the zone reads, the RPOs and the designed quarterback runs, the defense has to assign somebody to him before the snap. That extra defender has to come from somewhere, so every other call gets easier.

principles.title: THE RUN THREAT OPENS THE DEEP BALL
principles.blurb: Once they are honoring his legs, that is when we do the real damage down the field.
principles.detail: Once they are honoring his legs, that is when we do the real damage. All that run action pulls linebackers and safeties downhill. Then we throw play action right over the top of them into the space they just gave up.

principles.title: SPREAD THEM OUT, KEEP IT SIMPLE
principles.blurb: We live in the gun and spread you out sideline to sideline, and that does two things for us.
principles.detail: We live in the gun and spread you out sideline to sideline. It gives our quarterback clean, fast reads where he always knows where to go with the football. And it empties out the box, so there is nothing but green grass when he decides to take off.

plays.name: RPO Alert Draw Stick

reads.label: Stick Behind the Linebackers
reads.text: If everybody bites down on the draw, throw the little stick route as he sits down right in behind the linebackers. You can drop that in for big gains. It works against man too, because he breaks it outside and gets clean separation.

reads.label: Out Route, Wide Side
reads.text: If they are playing off zone, drop it in to your middle slot receiver on the wide side as he breaks out. Easy pitch and catch all day.

reads.label: Pull It and Go
reads.text: If everybody is playing back on the pass, or they bring a blitz and the middle of the field opens up, pull it and go with Jayden Daniels. Get him downhill in the open field and let him make people miss.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side
Middle receiver on the wide side to an out
Outside receiver on the wide side to a comeback
plays.whenToUse: This is the first play in the whole install and it is the one that tells you how they are playing your quarterback. A run, a quick answer behind the linebackers, and a pull all live on one snap, so you are never wrong. Call it early and read what they give you.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__RPO Alert Draw Stick Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN HB Wide Zone WK

reads.label: Edge Read
reads.text: Follow the TE motion blocker to the outside. If the edge stays open with the TE sealing the defender, turn the corner for big yardage.

reads.label: Cut Back Lane
reads.text: If the edge gets cut off, plant your foot immediately and get downhill through the cutback lane created by linebacker over-pursuit.

reads.label: Patience Read
reads.text: Be patient behind the zone blocking. Let the TE come all the way across and identify whether the crease opens outside or cuts back inside before committing.

plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need a reliable zone run with a built-in numbers advantage. That TE motion gives you an extra blocker at the point of attack. If they do not account for him, you are turning the corner for 30. If they do, you are cutting back all day.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__MTN HB Wide Zone WK Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Orbit RPO Peek Y Pop

reads.label: Pop Pass Behind the Linebackers
reads.text: The orbit motion swinging out to the flat widens the linebackers and the flat defenders. Key the linebackers in the middle: if they bite down on the run, hit the pop pass right in behind them. It gets to an amazing area of the field and it can be a big pickup over the middle.

reads.label: Hand It Off
reads.text: If at the snap the linebackers are all staying back and playing underneath that pop pass, just hand it off and get downhill with your running back. With those linebackers flat footed you should get some big pickups underneath.

adjustments: Tight end to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Run this when linebackers are getting nosy about the run. The orbit motion drags the flat defenders out of the picture and then the two linebackers in the middle have to pick one. Either answer is a good one for you.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Orbit RPO Peek Y Pop Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN Lead Toss

reads.label: Perimeter Leverage
reads.text: If defenders are pinned inside, the edge is open. Pitch it out and let the orbit motion blocker lead the way.

reads.label: Bunch Blockers
reads.text: The two receivers in the bunch block down, sealing the inside. Read whether they are winning their blocks before committing to the toss.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Run this when the defense is cheating inside and you can get to the perimeter. The orbit motion does the work. It builds momentum and puts a lead blocker on the edge before the snap even happens.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__MTN Lead Toss Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: HB MTN QB Sweep

reads.label: Get to the Edge
reads.text: This one is all about the perimeter. The bunch on that side locks the defense inside, and that lets you get out to the edge with your athletic quarterback where he can go make big plays.

reads.label: Cut It Back
reads.text: If the edge is taken away and they string it out, cut it back up the middle. They have committed everybody outside to stop the sweep, so the inside is there.

plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want the ball in Daniels hands in space. The bunch walls off the inside and everything after that is a footrace to the sideline. It is a red zone answer too, because the edge is a lot shorter down there.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__HB Mtn QB Sweep Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Pin Pull Sweep

reads.label: Edge Seal Read
reads.text: Read the playside puller’s block on the edge defender. If he is sealed inside, bounce it to the perimeter. If he is sealed outside, press the inside lane downhill.

reads.label: Safety Angle Read
reads.text: Once the edge is sealed, read the safety’s angle. If he takes a bad angle to the corner, beat him outside and turn upfield.

adjustments: Run to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to get to the perimeter with numbers. Two pullers out front means we are outnumbering the defense at the edge. If they cannot set the edge, this thing is gone.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Pin Pull Sweep Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Verts Dig

reads.label: Motioned Wheel
reads.text: Once you snap it, if the flat defender and the deep defender are just dropping back at the snap, fire it in to that wheel as he turns up the field and go get a bunch of easy yards.

reads.label: Tight End Wheel
reads.text: This is the go-to route on the play. If the flat defender widens out on that outside wheel and the linebackers stay inside on the deep cross, throw the tight end wheel as he cuts up the field. You can fire this in for a ton of big pickups.

reads.label: Deep Cross
reads.text: If the linebackers are widening out onto that tight end wheel, the deep cross is coming across the middle from the bunch. Fire it in over the middle, or wait until it gets in along the sideline.

reads.label: Checkdown, RB Swing
reads.text: Running back on the swing pass out in the flat when everything down the field is covered.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side
Middle receiver to a deep cross
Motion the outside receiver on the wide side out
plays.whenToUse: This is a zone shredder. Two wheels and a deep cross put the flat defender and the linebackers in a bind at the same time, and one of them is always wrong. The tight end wheel is the money route, so start your eyes outside and work back to it.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Verts Dig Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Hoss Y Juke

reads.label: Cover 3, Wide Side Seam
reads.text: Look to the wide side seam first. If the flat defender does not ride the slot receiver up the field, the seam is open. Linebackers tend to stay shallow for the tight end in the middle, leaving the wide side seam wide open.

reads.label: Cover 2, Wide Side Fade
reads.text: The trips slot streak holds the safety in the middle of the field. The outside receiver runs a fade behind the flat defender on the wide side. Hold the ball an extra half second to let the receiver get outside, then deliver the shot down the sideline.

reads.label: Cover 2, Short Side Post
reads.text: Against a two-high shell the short side seam converts to a post, breaking into the middle of the field away from the safety. Fire into the post window if the wide side fade is not there.

reads.label: Tight End Option
reads.text: Against zone, read the linebacker: if he stays shallow, throw the seam. If he drops under the seam, throw the tight end as he sits down. Against man, let the tight end declare his break, outside if the defender is inside leverage, inside drag if the defender is outside leverage.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side
Outside receiver on a streak
plays.whenToUse: Run this against any coverage. It attacks cover two, cover three and man all in one play. It is better than four verticals against cover three match because the option route forces the flat defender to choose between the hitch and the seam. Empty, trips wide, and you are in business.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Hoss Y Juke Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN Switch Verts

reads.label: The Motion Wheel
reads.text: An auto motion player comes across the field running a wheel up the sideline. Against zone, wait until he passes the flat defender. The streak on that side is pulling the deep defender back, and then you can drop this in for a big pickup. Against man, if his defender gets caught chasing him shallow across the field, fire it in.

reads.label: Either Seam
reads.text: Two seam routes are attacking, one on each side of the field. If the linebackers stay shallow, or guys are widening out on that wheel as he cuts up, take whichever seam is clean.

reads.label: Checkdown, the Slant
reads.text: Against zone, if everyone is dropping back under the seams and the wheel, throw the slant over the middle. Against man this is a really good option over the middle of the field too.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side
Outside receiver on the short side to a slant
plays.whenToUse: This is your shot play that still has a floor. The wheel is the home run, the two seams punish anybody who widens for it, and the slant means you are never taking a sack. Call it when you want to take a swing without gambling.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__MTN Switch Verts Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN Switch Comeback

reads.label: Outside Comeback, Short Side
reads.text: First look is the solo comeback on the short side. If the receiver gets separation breaking to the outside, fire it in immediately.

reads.label: Auto Motion Comeback, Wide Side
reads.text: Motion the slot across to the wide side. He runs a comeback underneath his trailing man coverage defender. With matching comebacks on both sides you have built-in answers to either edge.

reads.label: Post, No Middle Safety
reads.text: If you see no deep safety in the middle of the field, hit the slot receiver on the post breaking into the vacated space. Works down inside the 5-yard line.

reads.label: TE Drag or Dig
reads.text: Against pressure the tight end drag replaces where blitzing linebackers vacated in the middle. Or come back to the wide side dig running behind the motion comeback for a switch concept and a big pickup.

adjustments: Trips to the short side
Slot on a post on the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Run this against any man coverage look. Five routes, all beating man, so you are not reading a progression so much as finding who won. If they want to blitz, the TE drag punishes it. If there is no safety in the middle, the post is a touchdown.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Mtn Switch Comeback Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN FK Toss Verticals

reads.label: 1st Read, TE Wheel
reads.text: After the fake toss the tight end wheels up the sideline. The outside receiver’s streak clears out the deep defender on the short side, creating a window to drop the ball over the top along the sideline.

reads.label: 2nd Read, Deep Cross
reads.text: If the wheel does not look clean coming out of the backfield, check the point man running a deep cross from the bunch. If linebackers vacate the middle to chase the wheel or react to the fake toss, fire the crosser into that open window.

reads.label: 3rd Read, RB Swing
reads.text: If the defense is playing everything back and getting underneath the vertical routes, dump it to the running back on the swing route coming in behind the wheel.

adjustments: Bunch to the short side
Outside receiver on a streak to clear it out
plays.whenToUse: Run this as a package with the RPO alert swing and the lead toss, same motion, different outcomes. Best on third down when they are expecting run after seeing that toss action all game. The fake freezes everybody, and now you have a wheel, a cross and a swing all off the same look.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__MTN FK Toss Verticals Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Y Trail

reads.label: Corner Out from the Point Man
reads.text: The point man in the bunch gets up the field and breaks it outside. Once he has separation, fire it in. This is one of the more consistent routes on the whole play.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: The drag coming across the middle. If his man trails him or gets caught up in the bunch, that drag can get you a ton of big yards.

reads.label: TE Trail Route
reads.text: The tight end breaks out and then comes back in over the middle. He can get a ton of separation as he breaks back inside.

reads.label: Deep Post
reads.text: The deep post from the solo receiver, and this one is great if they have no deep safeties over the middle. If you have separation and nobody is back there, fire it up over the top.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side
Block the running back
Motion the solo post in
plays.whenToUse: This is an amazing man beater that gives you four ways to attack it. Everything in the bunch is designed to get somebody caught in traffic, and the trail route from the tight end is the one that keeps coming open when the rest is covered.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Y Trail Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Fade Smash

reads.label: 1st Read, Slot Fade
reads.text: The stemmed hitch pulls the deep defender back, freeing the slot on the fade behind the flat defender. Back-shoulder this along the sideline or the pylon, especially in the red zone.

reads.label: 2nd Read, TE Seam Post
reads.text: If the slot fade is covered, look to the tight end running a shallow seam post over the middle. If linebackers stay shallow and the flat defender bails too deep, drop it in over the middle.

reads.label: 3rd Read, Post Sit
reads.text: If the slot fade is taken away and linebackers crash under the TE route, the wide side receiver sits down on the post sit behind them. Make the linebackers choose between the TE and the post sit.

reads.label: Checkdown, RB Option
reads.text: Against zone the RB sits down in the open window. Against man he breaks outside and creates easy separation on linebackers. Safe, reliable checkdown when everything else is covered.

adjustments: Stem the hitch route up 4 to 5 notches, or put the outside receiver on a streak
Wide side receiver on a post sit
plays.whenToUse: Run this in the red zone when you need a high percentage shot with multiple answers. The slot fade is your bread and butter. If they take it away, the TE seam and the post sit will punish them, and the RB option is a safety valve against both man and zone.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Fade Smash Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Orbit PA Y Corner

reads.label: Corner Route vs Zone
reads.text: Read the flat defender. If he does not drop to 15 or 20 yards, throw the corner route as the receiver cuts upfield. Drop it in behind him for a big gain.

reads.label: Corner Route vs Man
reads.text: As the receiver cuts back to the outside he will have one on one separation. Pass lead it up and along the sideline over the top.

reads.label: Backside Dig
reads.text: If the defense overplays the corner route and leaves the middle open, fire the backside dig into the vacated pocket behind the linebackers.

reads.label: Checkdowns
reads.text: The orbit receiver releasing to the flat is the first checkdown. The RB on the option route sits against zone or breaks inside or outside against man as the second.

adjustments: Tight end to the wide side
Running back on an option route
Stem the outside receiver up 1 to 2 notches
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to use orbit motion to freeze linebackers and make them think RPO. It is a flood concept that attacks every level. The corner beats zone and man, the dig punishes anyone who overplays the outside, and you have two underneath checkdowns if they take it all away.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Orbit PA Y Corner Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Middle Hi Lo

reads.label: The Wheel, One Play Touchdown
reads.text: That motioned end route holds the deep third defenders inside against Cover 3 or Cover 2, and it lets the wheel get wide open down the sideline. Lead this up and away as far as you can and walk in scores over the top. Put a fast, athletic receiver on that wheel and you are just blowing right past them.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: If the wheel is taken away by the user, or they are playing Cover 4 or man, look to the post breaking in over the middle from the trips side. This one is great against match or man, attacking right in the middle of the field.

reads.label: Checkdown, the Hitch
reads.text: The inside player on the trips runs a little hitch. If everything is taken away deep, drop it into him underneath.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side
Outside receiver on the short side to a streak
Motion him in
plays.whenToUse: This is the best deep passing play in the whole scheme, 20.3 yards a call in testing. The motion holds the deep defenders inside and the wheel runs right past where they used to be. Save it for when you need seven, not three.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__Middle Hi Low Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: MTN RPO Alert Swing

reads.label: Perimeter Numbers
reads.text: Count defenders against blockers on the perimeter as the tight end goes through orbit motion. If you have more blockers than defenders, or equal with the ball carrier as an extra, flip it out to the swing.

reads.label: User Overreaction
reads.text: If the user chases the orbit motion and vacates the middle of the field, hand the ball off immediately and get downhill through the massive hole.

reads.label: Outnumbered Outside
reads.text: If you count three defenders on the perimeter against your blockers you do not have the numbers advantage. Hand it off up the middle and let the center get to the second level.

plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to stress the perimeter with orbit motion and punish whatever the defense gives you. They respect the swing, you hand it off. They crash on the run, you flip it out. Perfect in the red zone when every defender has to make a decision fast.
plays.heroShot: art/Commanders References__MTN RPO Alert Swing Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: RPO Read Flat Wheel

reads.label: Read Defender Crashes
reads.text: If the read defender crashes down on the running back at the snap, pull the ball and get to the perimeter with your athletic quarterback.

reads.label: Defense Sitting Back
reads.text: If the defense is not being aggressive pre-snap and playing off, hand it off to the running back.

reads.label: Tight End Crossing
reads.text: If defenders are crashing upfield into the quarterback’s face, or there is open grass outside, flip it out to the tight end crossing underneath. It turns into a screen with the post and the wheel acting as blockers.

adjustments: Slot receiver to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you have an athletic quarterback who can threaten the edge. The defense has to pick their poison: crash and give up the perimeter, or sit back and give up the run. Keep it simple, read the defender, pull or hand off, and only go to the tight end if you see a clear opportunity.

about.headline: WHO ARE THE PATRIOTS
copy: Two straight 4-13 seasons, and then Drake Maye took over. In 2025 New England went {rec|14-3}, worst to first in one year, and won the AFC East for the first time since 2019.
Maye threw for {yds|4,394 yards} and 31 touchdowns, and led the whole league in completion percentage, passer rating and QBR. He finished second in the MVP vote in one of the closest races in years.

Then he took the Patriots to the Super Bowl in his second season, and this offseason they put A.J. Brown beside him. The biggest arm of the three Young Guns with an elite weapon added, and the offense we are building is about pushing the ball down the field into tight windows.

principles.title: RUN IT, THEN FAKE IT
principles.blurb: A diverse run game and the play action that looks exactly like it. The Patriots run it to earn the shot, and so do we.
principles.detail: New England ran the ball to protect a young quarterback and to earn the play action, and a run game with a dozen looks keeps a defense honest all game. Every run had a play fake that looked identical, so the shot came off a picture the defense had already committed to. For us that means the defense never gets a clean read: duo, split zone, the jet and the read all carry a shot off the same motion, and the first time they jump the run the wheel is already gone.

principles.title: MAYE ON THE MOVE
principles.blurb: The rollouts, the boots and QB Zone. New England moves the pocket on purpose, and the defense has to fit his legs on every snap.
principles.detail: Maye is a big, athletic quarterback, and the Patriots moved the pocket on purpose to shorten the throw, get him away from the rush and add a runner the defense has to fit. A quarterback who might keep it is one more body the box has to account for on every snap. For us the legs are the answer when everything downfield is covered, and a user who has to worry about the quarterback is a user who is out of position for everything else.

principles.title: LET IT FLY
principles.blurb: The arm is why the Patriots built the offense around him, and it is why this one throws it deep on purpose.
principles.detail: In real life the arm is the whole reason New England rebuilt around him: he can drive the ball into windows most quarterbacks have to pass on, so the deep shot is always live and the coverage has to stay honest over the top. For us that arm turns a single high safety into a touchdown and a man defender in trail into a mesh wheel score. Because they have to respect the deep ball, the seams, the crossers and the checkdowns underneath open up for everything else in the book.

player.name: DRAKE MAYE
player.line: The arm that changed the franchise. Throws deep on the run.
player.bio: Third pick in the 2024 draft out of North Carolina. Took over the job as a rookie on a four win team, and in his second season threw for {yds|4,394 yards} and 31 touchdowns, led the league in completion percentage, passer rating and QBR, and finished second in the MVP vote. Went 14-3 and took the Patriots to the Super Bowl.
roleFor: The quarterback in this offense is the extra number. He reads the end on the RPOs and keeps it when the end crashes. He rolls out on purpose, so the throw is short and the rush is behind him. And when the shot is there he lets it fly, because the whole scheme is built to earn that one throw.
Everything on the call sheet asks him to do one of three things: read, move, or throw it over the top. That is why the arm and the legs matter more here than in any other Young Gun offense.

plays.name: DBL Mtn Duo Wrap

reads.label: Follow the Lead Blocker
reads.text: The receiver motions across, then motions right back, so at the snap he is coming across at full speed as your lead blocker. Let him get there first and run behind him.

reads.label: The Aim Point Is Up the Gut
reads.text: It is duo up front with multiple double teams, so the normal aim point is right up the gut. Read the double teams and get downhill.

reads.label: Bounce It
reads.text: With that lead blocker kicking guys out, this one bounces better than a normal duo. When everybody gets pinned inside, turn the corner and loop around the user.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: Run this early and run it often. It sets up DBL Mtn PA Stretch, which uses the identical motion, so every time they start jumping the back, the wheel is waiting. Good anywhere, and a goal line call.

plays.name: DBL Mtn PA Stretch

reads.label: The Wheel Against Zone
reads.text: The motion man comes around, then wheels back up the field out of the backfield behind a hard play fake. The streak from the middle of the bunch pulls the deep defenders back. The second he clears behind the flat defender, let it fly over the top.

reads.label: The Wheel Against Man
reads.text: His man follows him across, but when he cuts back the defender is slow to react and has to run through every linebacker in the middle. He gets caught flat footed and the wheel turns up the field on him.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: If the wheel is covered, look deep over the middle. The streak runs the deep defenders off, and with no linebackers in the middle the post is a hole shot. Against man he separates at the break.

reads.label: The Whip
reads.text: The checkdown. The tight end runs a whip underneath into the flat, and you let him make a play in the open field.

adjustments: Bunch to the short side of the field
Middle player in the bunch on a streak
Tight end (the inside bunch player) on a whip
Solo outside receiver on a post
plays.whenToUse: The shot that lives on top of DBL Mtn Duo Wrap. The motion is identical, so call it the first time you see the user and the linebackers jumping down on the run. It works against zone and man.

plays.name: Jet Pass FK Zone

reads.label: Flip It
reads.text: The slot comes across on the jet motion and you flip it to him. The edge gets sealed, everybody gets caught inside, and your playmaker turns the corner with the ball.

reads.label: One Man to Beat
reads.text: Most of the time there is one defender left on the perimeter. Make him miss and it is a touchdown.

reads.label: Run It First
reads.text: Five plays in this offense use this jet motion. Run this one a few times first so the user and the linebackers start jumping down on it, and it opens up everything else.

adjustments: Tight ends to the wide side of the field
Your best receiver in the slot running the motion
plays.whenToUse: The first call in the jet family. Everything else out of this formation, the duo, the cross screen, the fake jet wheel and the sprint slide, is built on the defense chasing this. Great inside the 15 too.

plays.name: Jet Sprint HB Slide

reads.label: Flow One Way, Routes the Other
reads.text: The jet motion pulls the linebackers and the user toward it, and every route on the play goes the opposite way. The built-in rollout gets Maye out on the perimeter where he makes plays.

reads.label: The Deep Post
reads.text: The streak runs off the deep defenders and the post comes in behind them. Hit it whenever it is there, against zone or man.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: If the deep post is taken away, the shallower cross runs away from his man underneath it. Drop it in and let him run.

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: When everybody plays back on the two crossers, the back is leaking out in front of you as you roll. One on one, make a guy miss, first down.

adjustments: Tight ends to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: Call it once the defense has started flowing to the jet motion. The whole flow goes one way and the routes and the rollout go the other, so the middle of the field is empty when the post comes across.

plays.name: QB Zone

reads.label: The Edge Gets Sealed
reads.text: The tight ends kick out, the running back leads, the tackle climbs to the second level. Everybody gets sealed inside, so most of the time you bounce it and there is nothing but grass on the perimeter.

reads.label: One on One With the Safety
reads.text: The double team on the edge comes off and the second tight end picks up the safety. Beat one man and it is a fifty yard run.

reads.label: Straight Up
reads.text: You can also just run it straight up. The blocking on this play is as good as any run in the scheme.

reads.label: The Motion, or Not
reads.text: Motion the slot across to match the jet look. Against zone nobody follows him and you buy a blocker; against man it cancels out. Sometimes leave him home so the user has no tell you are coming.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
Optional: motion the slot receiver across the formation
plays.whenToUse: The favorite run in the whole scheme. It needs an athletic quarterback, and that is the point of this offense. Call it in the red zone and on any down you need the edge.

plays.name: Dash Flood

reads.label: The Back in the Flat
reads.text: Dash means a designed rollout to the bunch side. The first place to look is the back. If the end is in your face, everybody is caught inside, or it is zone and they all play back, drop it to him right away and let him rip up the sideline.

reads.label: The Corner Over the Flat
reads.text: The corner route is deep. The flat defender stops at ten yards and needs to get to twenty to take it away, and the rollout shortens the throw. Drop it in along the sideline.

reads.label: The Backside Cross
reads.text: Against man, or against zone when the linebackers leave the middle for the roll side, the shallow cross comes across from the short side. This is why you want an elite weapon: get him the ball and let him go.

reads.label: The Whip
reads.text: The whip breaks in then out. Good against man, or into a little pocket on the backside against zone.

reads.label: Pull It and Go
reads.text: You are already out of the pocket. If everything is covered and they are caught inside, use the legs and take ten yards.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Tight end on a streak, then motion him out
plays.whenToUse: Five answers on one play, with the rollout built in. One of the favorites in the whole scheme: the back, the corner, the cross, the whip, and Maye running when they get caught inside.

plays.name: Shallow Cross Bomb

reads.label: Against Cover 3
reads.text: The tight end streak holds the middle safety in the middle of the field. The post sit holds the backside deep third down. The post comes up over the top of all of it, and you bomb him for a walk in touchdown.

reads.label: Against Cover 1 and Match
reads.text: The deep safety is still held in the middle, and the backside man is held by the post sit. If the post has separation, fire it up over the top untouched.

reads.label: The Post Sit
reads.text: Against two high, or a Cover 3 where the safety is not pulled, come off the shot. The flat and the hook bite down and the post sit sits down in the zone. Drop it in.

reads.label: The Swing
reads.text: If the flat defender plays back under the post sit, the back is on the swing. Put it in his hands.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Tight end on a streak
plays.whenToUse: A one play touchdown against Cover 3, and it works against Cover 1 too. Take it the first time you see a single high safety, and live on the post sit and the swing when they go two high.

plays.name: Mesh

reads.label: The Mesh Wheel
reads.text: The tight end runs a unique wheel out of the mesh. His defender shoots down on it or gets caught in the natural pick of the two drags, ends up in a trail position, and you throw it up over the top for one play touchdowns.

reads.label: The Drags
reads.text: Out of a condensed set the man players start in an outside shade, so the drags are already running away from a trailing defender. Three or four yards of separation before he even breaks.

reads.label: The Drags Against Zone
reads.text: If they switch to zone, the drags sit down in the soft spot instead of running into the flat defenders. Easy checkdowns.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: No safety help, fire it at the break. Split safeties, put it in between them. Single high, wait for him to clear and lead it away.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Block the running back
plays.whenToUse: The go to man beater in the scheme, and one of the best in the game. If they are spamming man, this and In Quick Outs are the two calls. The wheel alone is worth a touchdown a game.

plays.name: Hop Split Zone

reads.label: The Hop
reads.text: The back starts offset beside the quarterback and hops in behind him. The offset sets the strength of the defense, then you run back to the bunch side away from it.

reads.label: Split Zone
reads.text: The tight end kicks back across the formation and the line and the bunch players climb to the second level. Everybody gets pinned inside.

reads.label: Bounce or Cut
reads.text: Turn the corner when the edge is sealed, or cut it right up the middle when the lane is there. This run goes the distance.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The same hop motion as Hop PA Boot Slide, so the two work off each other. Establish this one and the boot has all the grass it wants.

plays.name: MTN RPO Read Y Slide

reads.label: Read the End
reads.text: The auto motion comes across at the snap and you read the defensive end. If he crashes on the back, keep it and get out into the open field. If they overplay the edge, cut it back inside.

reads.label: The Give
reads.text: If the end stays home and you see the hole up the middle, give it and let the back get downhill.

reads.label: The Slide
reads.text: You pulled it and somebody is coming off on you or looping around. The tight end is coming across the formation into the flat. Drop it out to him and let him make a play.

reads.label: The Slot Wheel
reads.text: No flat defender on the wide side and everybody playing back: throw the slot wheel early.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: A read option with two throws attached. Read the end first, then the slide and the wheel are there when the defense starts cheating to the quarterback.

plays.name: Hop PA Boot Slide

reads.label: The Deep Post
reads.text: The same hop motion as the split zone, then a hard play fake and the boot out the other side. The streak pulls everyone back, the linebackers and the flat stay shallow, and the post gets to twenty five yards. Throw it up.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: When the deep cross is taken away, everybody bit on the fake and the middle is empty. The shallower cross comes in behind them for fifteen or twenty.

reads.label: The Flat
reads.text: Beat the edge on the boot. If everybody plays back under the two crossers, check it to the tight end in the flat and get up the field.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Solo receiver on a streak (clears everyone out)
plays.whenToUse: Call it after Hop Split Zone has hit a few times. They crash the run, you boot out the other way with three levels in front of you.

plays.name: Seattle

reads.label: The Outside Wheel
reads.text: Look before the snap. If the corner is off and the flat defender is inside, quick throw the wheel as he cuts up the field. That is a free twenty yards.

reads.label: The Crosser
reads.text: If a defender jumps the wheel, come inside to the crosser. Against man he runs away from his defender; against zone there is a pocket between the widened defenders, or wait for him to clear behind the flat.

reads.label: The Tight End Wheel
reads.text: The outside wheel pulls the flat defender out and the linebackers get pulled inside, so the tight end wheel goes up the seam untouched. Quick throw it as he cuts, or let him carry it vertical.

reads.label: The Back
reads.text: If you do not like any of the verticals, the back is on an option route. He sits down against zone and breaks in or out against man.

adjustments: Bunch to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver in the bunch (the wheel) motioned out
Running back on an option route
plays.whenToUse: Four verticals out of the bunch with easy reads: look to the three bunch routes, check it to the back. Off coverage means the wheel is free before the ball is even snapped.

plays.name: Jet HB Duo

reads.label: They Chase the Jet
reads.text: Run the touch pass a few times first. Now the user and the linebackers leave the middle of the field to take the jet motion.

reads.label: Downhill
reads.text: Hand it off up the middle and attack downhill into the holes they just opened. It only gets better the more they overplay the outside.

reads.label: Make One Man Miss
reads.text: Get through the hole, make a guy miss, and it is nine or ten yards a pop.

adjustments: Tight ends to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The inside run of the jet family. Once they are overplaying the touch pass to the outside, this hits straight up the gut.

plays.name: Jet HB Cross Screen

reads.label: Flow to the Jet
reads.text: The jet motion pulls the linebackers and the user out of the middle toward the wide side, and the slip screen to the back goes the other way.

reads.label: Buy Half a Second
reads.text: Sitting in the pocket does not give the screen time to set up. Take off a little, buy the linemen half a second to get out in front of the back.

reads.label: Drop It Out
reads.text: Two linemen in front, drop it in to the back, and let him make one man miss. That is twenty five or thirty yards up the sideline.

adjustments: Tight ends to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The screen in the jet family. Everybody leaves the middle to chase the motion and the back has blockers in space going the other way.

plays.name: Fake Jet HB Wheel

reads.label: The Fake Pulls the User
reads.text: The jet comes across and the linebackers and the user bite down on it. Watch the user leave the middle of the field.

reads.label: The Inside Tight End
reads.text: The inside tight end runs vertical into the hole the user just left. Throw it over the linebacker who stays shallow and high point it.

reads.label: The Outside Tight End
reads.text: The outside tight end goes up the seam. Same thing: when they step down to the motion, put it over their heads.

reads.label: The Back on the Wheel
reads.text: The back leaks out on a vertical. If the flat defender stays shallow, or it is man, throw the wheel in behind the linebacker.

reads.label: The Checkdown
reads.text: If everybody plays vertical and gets under the three routes, check it to the jet motion player and live to fight another down.

adjustments: Tight ends to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: Three vertical routes leaving together behind the jet fake. The more the defense has been burned by the touch pass, the more of the middle of the field they give you.

plays.name: 0-1 Trap

reads.label: The Pulling Guard
reads.text: A down block, a double team up to the second level, and the guard pulls across the center to kick out the trap defender.

reads.label: Wait for Him to Engage
reads.text: Let the trap defender engage the puller, then put your foot in the ground and get up the field for eight or nine.

reads.label: Do Not Bounce It
reads.text: Shotgun traps hit hard and hit quick right up the middle. Read the puller and get downhill.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
plays.whenToUse: The one run out of Tight Y Off Wk. It is a passing formation, but every formation needs a run, and this one hits fast up the middle.

plays.name: Shuffle HB Choice

reads.label: The Seams Against Cover 3
reads.text: Both streaks get free releases up the seams, nobody jams. Single high safety over the tight end means the outside streak is open up his seam. If they blitz off the tight end side or the safety overplays, take the tight end seam instead.

reads.label: Against Cover 2
reads.text: The tight end splits the two safeties up the middle, or the slot fade gets behind the flat defender while the streak holds the deep half inside. Either one is a touchdown.

reads.label: The Back Against Zone
reads.text: The back is on an option route: he sits down or breaks to the outside. He is the checkdown most of the time.

reads.label: Against Man
reads.text: The whip breaks in then out, or the back options out of the backfield and runs a Texas route into the middle of the field, wide open.

adjustments: Running back to the short side of the field
Tight end on a streak
Outside receiver of the tight look (short side) on a streak
plays.whenToUse: Attack the seams. Two free releases against Cover 3, two touchdowns against Cover 2, and the back and the whip answer man.

plays.name: In Quick Outs

reads.label: The Speed Out
reads.text: The outside receiver on the tight side runs a quick speed out. The outside leverage defender shoots inside, he fires out, and he gets two, three, four yards of separation every time. Rack catch, make a guy miss, up the sideline.

reads.label: The Slant
reads.text: Not a stock slant: he attacks outside first and then breaks in, so he gets way better separation than a normal slant. With nobody in the middle, drop it in.

reads.label: The Out on the Wide Side
reads.text: He goes hard inside then breaks out. Not always a lot of separation, but you can throw it up along the sideline for the first down.

reads.label: The Tight End Post
reads.text: After the snap, if they have no safeties over the top, the tight end post breaks into the middle of the field. Fire it in and turn it up.

adjustments: Tight end to the short side of the field (two tight receivers to the wide side)
Block the running back
Tight end on a post
plays.whenToUse: One of the two man beaters in the scheme. When they are spamming man, the speed out is money, and the slant and the post are right beside it.
